test.name: Under the step gate, a bounded first message with a PID runs its search in the turn that creates the project
test.description: ut_research_b4i under execution.step_mode step, the prototype worker's gate. Before PR for issue #2813, a turn opened by init-project fixed the setup group and denied the search; the validator reads that denial off the search's returned text. Now the step after init-project fixes the group (plan section H).

input.user_message: /research Can you find records for Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF, that aren't attached to his FamilySearch record yet?

judge_context: A bounded first message (finding a record) with a FamilySearch ID and no project. The router creates the project with init-project, which runs for real here, and then runs the record search in the SAME turn: no question-selection, locality-guide or research-plan first (issue #2813, feedback #4237).

The reply must end on a "Continue with …?" offer; which step it offers is the router's call, and the offered step is not one the turn should have run. It must leave out init-project's sentence about a first research question. Both, with the hand-offs, the tree id handed as the search subject and the absence of a step denial, are checked deterministically by test_bounded_first_message_runs_its_deliverable_after_init_project. Do not re-grade them.

search-records is stubbed: the transcript shows no record_search calls because the stub returned a canned report that found nothing new, and relaying that report as the searches done is correct. Grade the reply on relaying that honestly and on saying the project was made. Mark it down for naming any site, archive or record set (Ancestry, newspapers) that no tool returned.
Do not mark the reply down for not writing a research question, a plan or a locality survey: on a bounded ask those are the failure this test exists to catch.
